To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• the neutron fluence in the JET tokamak is high enough to induce damage in the image sensors of cameras; • the neutron fluences at the camera locations are not uniform; • the radiation damage to the sensors depends on the neutron energy spectrum; • the neutron damage to the image sensors is cumulative; • the damage to the sensors increases the dark current and increases the number of defective pixels; • the radiation induced dark current and hot-pixel count increase linearly with the neutron fluence
the neutron radiation damage to the camera sensors is a function of the neutron fluence and that the damage is proportional to the neutron fluence.
